hook.line: A good argument admits what is true before it pushes back. That is what makes people trust you, and Spanish has small words for each step.
hook.es: Es cierto que necesitamos dinero, pero no a cualquier precio.
hook.en: It's true that we need money, but not at any price.

examples.es: Es cierto que necesitamos dinero, pero no a cualquier precio.
examples.en: It's true that we need money, but not at any price.
In fact, sales are going up.

rule:
Four small tools:

*Es cierto que…, pero…*: admit a point, then push back. The fact after *que* is plain and in the indicative.
*De hecho*: "in fact", backing up what you just said with something real.
*No solo… sino también…*: not only this but also that. After a *no solo*, English "but" becomes *sino*.
*En cambio*: "on the other hand", setting two people or things side by side.

English "actually" is not *actualmente* here; use *de hecho*.
smallPrint: Teachers call these discourse markers, or connectors: they show how one idea relates to the next.

readAndPick.es: Es cierto que necesitamos dinero, pero no a cualquier precio.
options: It's true we need money, but not at any price.
We need money, and at any price.
It's not true that we need money.

readAndPick.es: No solo es barato, sino también práctico.
options: It's cheap, not practical.
It's not only cheap but also practical.
It isn't cheap but it is practical.

readAndPick.es: Ellos quieren vender; nosotros, en cambio, queremos quedarnos.
options: They want to sell, so we want to stay.
They and we both want to change.
They want to sell; we, on the other hand, want to stay.
In fact, sales are going up.
Of course, sales are going down.
Sales went up, but now they are down.

readAndPick.es: No solo vienen turistas, sino también vecinos.
options: Tourists come, but neighbors don't.
Not only tourists come, but also neighbors.
Neither tourists nor neighbors come.

readAndPick.es: Es verdad que el edificio es viejo, pero tiene historia.
options: The building is old because it has history.
The building is old, so it has no history.
It's true the building is old, but it has history.

readAndPick.es: Tomás quiere abrir; Vale, en cambio, quiere esperar.
options: Tomás wants to open; Vale, on the other hand, wants to wait.
Tomás wants to open because Vale wants to wait.
Tomás and Vale both want to wait.

readAndPick.es: De hecho, mucha gente ya lo sabe.
options: Of course, many people don't know it yet.
In fact, many people already know it.
Many people know it, but only in part.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *___ necesitamos dinero, pero no a cualquier precio.* (*Es cierto que* or *De hecho*) It's true that we need money, but not at any price.
yourTurn.answer: Es cierto que necesitamos dinero, pero no a cualquier precio.
yourTurn.why: You admit the point first, so *es cierto que*, then *pero* turns it.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *No solo es barato, ___ también práctico.* (*sino* or *pero*) It's not only cheap but also practical.
yourTurn.answer: No solo es barato, sino también práctico.
yourTurn.why: After *no solo*, the matching word is *sino*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: In fact, sales are going up.
yourTurn.why: *De hecho* adds a real fact that backs up your point.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: They want to sell; we, on the other hand, want to stay.
yourTurn.answer: Ellos quieren vender; nosotros, en cambio, queremos quedarnos.
yourTurn.why: *En cambio* sets the two sides against each other.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: It's true that the building is old, but it has history.
yourTurn.answer: Es verdad que el edificio es viejo, pero tiene historia.
accept: Es cierto que el edificio es viejo, pero tiene historia.
yourTurn.why: You admit one point, then *pero* brings the other.

yourTurn.prompt: Add a concession: *El plan es caro, pero es justo.* Start with *Es cierto que*.
yourTurn.answer: Es cierto que el plan es caro, pero es justo.
yourTurn.why: *Es cierto que* admits the first half before the *pero*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say not only one thing: *Vienen turistas y vecinos.* Use *no solo… sino también*.
yourTurn.answer: No solo vienen turistas, sino también vecinos.
yourTurn.why: *No solo* opens the first part and *sino también* adds the second.

pitfalls.wrong: No solo es barato, pero también práctico.
pitfalls.right: No solo es barato, sino también práctico.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After *no solo*, the "but also" half uses *sino*, not *pero*.

pitfalls.wrong: Es cierto que el plan es caro y es justo.
pitfalls.right: Es cierto que el plan es caro, pero es justo.
pitfalls.why: Almost. A concession needs *pero* to turn the argument.

pitfalls.wrong: Es cierto que el plan sea caro, pero es justo.
pitfalls.right: Es cierto que el plan es caro, pero es justo.
pitfalls.why: Almost. You are admitting a fact, so use the indicative, not the subjunctive.

pitfalls.wrong: En el cambio, nosotros queremos quedarnos.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *En cambio* has no article, and it sits right after the thing you contrast.

personal: Think of a place you know well. Make one honest concession and push back: *Es cierto que… pero…*.
